pocket_rule: CONTACT THAT GIVES WAY DOES NOT CANCEL MOMENTUM. THE ROOT MUST CHASE THE TARGET BEFORE SUPPORT CAN BRAKE.

source.identity: Guile — Super Street Fighter II: The New Challengers — SNES — Fighters
observed: complete static fighter sheet with neutral/travel/crouch/airborne anchors and close/far grounded attacks
horizontal reach is purchased by torso/root commitment before or with distal extension
recovery is structurally distinct from simple reverse playback and negative space changes with attack state
inferred: contact pin while target gives way

compile.connector_semantics: inherits nearer authored endpoint; no invented support/contact/target events

keys.name: ASYMMETRIC_READY
keys.motion_arc_root_note: root stacked behind split base; guard closes rear corridor while strike hand floats forward

keys.name: COIL_REAR_LOAD
keys.motion_arc_root_note: root drops rearward and torso folds away from strike corridor; strike arm compresses instead of translating

keys.name: ROOT_COMMIT_BRIDGE
keys.motion_arc_root_note: pelvis advances before distal hand; shoulders unwind into a rising diagonal

keys.name: PRECONTACT_SURGE
keys.motion_arc_root_note: root and shoulder line surge into threat lane; hand is short of target while body commitment is already paid

keys.name: CONTACT_INSTANT
keys.support_contact: front braces while rear still drives
keys.motion_arc_root_note: distal hand reaches target while pelvis is still advancing; impact does not freeze root

keys.name: YIELD_PIN_ROOT_OVERRUN
keys.support_contact: front catches first overrun; rear lightens
keys.motion_arc_root_note: target and hand travel together while root continues through contact; torso compresses behind moving distal point
keys.target_note: target yields from x55 to x58 while contact remains pinned

keys.name: CHASE_STEP_LAUNCH
keys.support_contact: rear support catches root while front foot chases
keys.motion_arc_root_note: because target kept yielding, base can no longer brake in old place; front support leaves ground while torso remains committed
keys.target_note: target yields again to x61; fist stays pinned

keys.name: CHASE_STEP_CATCH
keys.support_contact: front support lands forward and owns brake
keys.motion_arc_root_note: new front contact catches translated root; strike arm remains loaded into yielded target for one beat
keys.target_note: target gives last unit to x62 under pinned contact

keys.name: TARGET_RELEASE_ARM_OVERRUN
keys.motion_arc_root_note: target stops yielding and contact breaks; distal hand overruns past target while pelvis is finally checked by new front support
keys.target_note: target stays at x62; hand passes to x64 after release

keys.name: PELVIS_COUNTERBRAKE
keys.support_contact: dual support; front still primary brake
keys.motion_arc_root_note: pelvis reverses first against new base while shoulder/hand remain forward; internal braking wave begins proximal-to-distal

keys.name: SHOULDER_HAND_LAG
keys.motion_arc_root_note: root has already traveled back while strike shoulder and hand are still finishing forward/downward arc

keys.name: RECOIL_OVERSHOOT
keys.support_contact: rear support catches recoil; front searches
keys.motion_arc_root_note: strike hand retracts past torso after root brake, making recoil visibly overshoot rather than mirror the launch

keys.name: FRONT_SUPPORT_LAG_CATCH
keys.support_contact: front settles late into widened displaced base
keys.motion_arc_root_note: root restacks while strike arm rebounds from overshoot; front support completes recovery one beat later

keys.name: DISPLACED_READY
keys.support_contact: dual support restored in forward-shifted stance
keys.motion_arc_root_note: body settles well forward of K00; yielded contact permanently spent a chase step

quality_thesis: A yielding target changes the recovery bill: contact first occurs before maximum body travel, then hand and target remain pinned together while root overruns; the yielded target forces a chase step before a new support point can brake the body; release produces distal overrun, proximal counter-braking, shoulder/hand lag, recoil overshoot, and a displaced settle rather than reverse interpolation.

observations: K01 folds root rearward before any distal commitment; K02-K03 visibly advance pelvis before the hand reaches the target.
K04 is a distinct first-contact key before maximum body travel.
K05-K07 pin strike hand to the yielding target while root overruns and the front support launches then catches farther forward.
K08 releases only after the chase-step catch; distal hand overruns the now-stationary target.
K09-K13 brake proximal-first, preserve shoulder/hand lag, overshoot past the torso, then settle in a forward-displaced base.

noodle_queen.taste: The target visibly drags the body into an uglier, longer obligation instead of rewarding contact with a clean snapback.
noodle_queen.function: Yield, root overrun, chase-step launch/catch, release, proximal brake, distal lag, overshoot, and displaced recovery read as one causal chain.
noodle_queen.contempt: Not a mannequin translation, endpoint tap, planted-feet pantomime, mirrored reversal, or metadata-only target yield.
